claims.sentence: References to works that do not exist were found in 53 papers accepted at NeurIPS 2025 \citep{ansari2026compound}, and a scan of the 2025 papers accepted at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS and USENIX Security estimated that 0.38--0.81\% of their references were likely hallucinated \citep{russinovich2026phantom}.
claims.claim: A scan of 2025 accepted papers at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS and USENIX Security estimated that 0.38-0.81% of their references were likely hallucinated.
claims.excerpt: For the latest complete year, 2025, the all-reference rate is 0.38% at ICLR, 0.54% at ICML, 0.68% at NeurIPS, and 0.81% at USENIX Security
claims.note: Supported. Minor: 0.38-0.81% is the range of per-venue all-reference rates (0.31-0.55% over academic-paper-like references only); the corpus covers 'every accepted paper we could retrieve' and 'likely hallucinated' includes substantial author-list mismatches as well as unfound works. The authors also say false-positive noise dominates at the reference level, which the manuscript's 'estimated ... likely' adequately hedges.
